name: Ink-Grinding Primer (Ma Mặc Quyết)
concept: The outer gate grinds ink before it is allowed to paint. Each stroke of the inkstick on the stone is one breath, and the breath goes into the ink: Water from the well water, Wood from the agarwood soot. After six layers the ink holds qi for a day, and a brush line drawn with it can be pushed a hand's width through the air. The novice fights the way a calligrapher writes, with short wet strokes, and wins by not stopping.
lore: Kha Đạm Mặc wrote it in 905 for the first island children who came to the abbey, because, he said, a child who will not grind ink will not wait for a cloud.

name: Idle Cloud Reflection Canon (Nhàn Vân Đàm Ảnh Kinh)
concept: The cultivator learns to be the still pool of Đàm Ảnh Thành: to hold what passes over without holding on to it. Qi settles in the dantian like water after wind, and whatever crosses it leaves a reflection. In a fight the painter paints her own reflection out of that stillness, a double in wet ink that stands beside her and takes blows, and the longer the fight stays calm the better the double holds. It is a patient, defensive method. It is weak against a rush and very hard to wear down.
lore: Diệp Tố Quyên and Kha Đạm Mặc wrote it out between 905 and 960 from what they had learned painting the sky upside down in the pool (A152, V092). The abbey says it is not finished and never will be.

name: Living Scroll Art (Hoạt Quyển Thuật)
concept: The painting of things that move. On bamboo paper from the abbey's mill, a figure painted in qi-ink can walk inside its scroll and, for a few breaths, step off it. Wood gives the figure its life and Water its ink. The abbey lives on this art: it sells door scrolls whose painted guardians step down at night, and boat scrolls whose painted carp swim ahead of a hull to find the deep channel. In a fight the painter unrolls a scroll and lets what is on it out.
lore: The founder's door scrolls were the abbey's first trade, sold in Triều Âm Thành from 910. Since 1158 the abbey teaches it with one rule: never paint a living face onto the scroll, only its reflection.

name: Painting the Old Reflection (Họa Cựu Ảnh Pháp)
concept: Kha Đạm Mặc believed the pool of Đàm Ảnh Thành keeps every sky it has ever held, layer on layer like sediment, and that a painter with enough stillness can paint an old one back out. This is his method for doing it. In a fight it paints the foe's reflection from a few seconds before and sets the foe back into it: their newest wards and buffs are lost, and any blow they struck in those seconds is undone on the painter. It is slow to cast and costly, and the abbey says that every time it is used something of the painter goes into the water.
lore: Kha taught it to two people, Diệp Tố Quyên and Mễ Phù Vân, and died in 1010 at the pool's edge with half the sky of 705 on his silk (N-nhan_van-02). Tần Đảo Ảnh has not been taught it and is trying it anyway.
